# IPaper
IPaper is an academic paper-writing product bundle for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). The publishable packa
ge, `@ai4paper/dsh-ipaper`, contributes academic presets, paper-project tools and views, and brandin
g to upstream DSH Web `0.2.2-rc.1`. APaper supplies the profile-root academic toolkit.
## Install, run, and update
Use DSH `0.2.2-rc.1` and pnpm 11. APaper `0.2.3` requires a profile-local override so its MCP adapte
r shares the supported DSH runtime. For a new profile, create this configuration before installing:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Install upstream Web before IPaper; APaper remains a separate direct dependency:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The profile's bundle order is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`, then `@ai4paper/d
sh-ipaper`. The CLI and APaper are plain dependencies, not bundles. Launch and manage the installed
product through its profile-local CLI to keep DSH service identities shared. To update or remove the
hrough its profile-local CLI to keep DSH service identities shared. To update or remove the product:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Preserve the profile override during updates; merge it into an existing workspace file rather than r
eplacing other settings. Restart DSH and refresh the browser page after updates. See the migration r
eference before updating an existing fork-based profile.
## Development and validation
Requires Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`, pnpm 11.7.0, and a configured DSH model provider.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`pnpm dev` builds IPaper, provisions the development profile, and runs the product-client watcher be
side DSH. Upstream Web supplies the shell and standard plugins; IPaper builds only its product plugi
ns and branding assets. The shell requires DSH-injected `window.__DSH_BOOT__`. Browser authenticatio
n defaults on; local browser automation can disable it through the connection adapter configuration.
Each dev launch uses an OS-assigned available port and DSH prints its browser URL, so concurrent lau
nches do not compete for port 3080. To request a fixed port, use `pnpm dev --port 3081` or `npm run
dev -- --port 3081`.
## Built-in preset
`ipaper` is the supported built-in agent preset: read-only, system-trust, and the default for new se
ssions. It includes IPaper's `find-the-problem` skill and activates APaper, providing `writing`, `cr
eating-figures`, and literature-research tools. The persona preserves author intent and prohibits fa
bricated citations, quotations, bibliographic metadata, data, and results. Users can manually copy t
he preset into the writable user root, customize it, and restart DSH; the package README describes t
he procedure. General and code-agent system roots are excluded.
Select `/find-the-problem` from the composer or **Start guided workflow** in Paper status to begin l
ive search, shortlisting, boundary mapping, gap verification, and interest/novelty/feasibility selec
earch, shortlisting, boundary mapping, gap verification, and interest/novelty/feasibility selection.
## Architecture and extensions
The product Cordis patch extends upstream Web with academic presets, branding, and Paper status. One
host-owned `paperProjects` service stores shared research memory for each workspace: sources, findi
ngs, and notes with references, session attribution, optimistic versions, and atomic commits. The `i
paper_record` and `ipaper_state` tools expose memory to root agents and append-only subagents. Paper
status shows counts, recent records, and author-marked unresolved questions. Manuscripts and workin
g plans remain ordinary workspace files.
The shared research memory design describes the architecture and automatic migration from the earlie
r graph. Migration preserves a complete legacy snapshot and the original graph storage; old graph to
ol payloads are rejected. See the tool contract and storage limitations.
Extensions remain separate profile-root packages and use upstream public service, RPC, and browser-s
lot contracts. The package README defines the extension recipe and package-specific runtime details.
